newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end with big gain, cheered by Dow.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end with big gain, cheered by Dow.

text.p: French shares closed on Monday on a strong note, but failed to break through resistance at 2,306, as gains on Wall Street boosted the CAC-40 index, traders said.

Dollar strength, which helps investment inflows, and hopes of continued French interest rate cuts supported the Paris market. But recent sharp swings on the U.S. Dow Jones index also induced a note of caution.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 23.91 points or 1.05 percent at 2,306.67, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,316 from 2,304 on Friday's settle.
The market is also being pushed up by buy orders from fund managers and marketmakers adding stock at the start of the month as normal business resumes after the holidays.
U.S. producer prices on Thursday and employment figures on Friday will hold the market's gaze in case a wild card comes up.
Utility group Cie Generale des Eaux tops the actives list, gaining 3.61 percent to 661 francs as market welcomes asset sales and debt reduction news.
Insurer Axa completed sale of near-five percent stake in retailer Galeries Lafayette. Axa has been reported to be considering selling other minority stakes.
Chemicals company Rhone-Poulenc sheds 1.21 percent to 171.40 francs, after brokerage Goldman Sachs marked the stock down to market performer from outperformer.
Industrial gases group Air Liquide climbs 2.54 percent to 807 francs, following an upgrade from CCF Elysees Bourse which sees a target of 1,000 francs for the share price.
Dollar earners rise, including LVMH, up 2.19 percent to 1,444 francs, Elf Aquitaine up 1.31 percent to 477.7 and Total up 1.44 percent to 422.
